newsitem.title: UK: European vegetable oil ends quiet session mixed.
newsitem.headline: European vegetable oil ends quiet session mixed.

text.p: European vegetable oil prices finished a quiet session on Monday mixed with palm oil under pressure from rising production while soft oils were supported by a stronger dollar.
A bearish report by Malaysian private forecaster Ivan Wong put palm oil prices under further pressure in Europe.
Ivan Wong projected end-March Malaysian palm oil output at 663,000 tonnes, 32 percent up from end-February.
Wong put stocks at 725,000 tonnes against the Malaysian Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority's (PORLA) 722,993 tonnes at end-February.
Exports were estimated at 560,000 tonnes against 376,885 tonnes during February.
Traders said although the figures were bearish the nearby market remains steady.
"People are only buying spot material because they expect prices to fall, but sellers do not have much room to manoeuvre when they try to replace material," said one.
A strong dollar continued to support soft oils with the higher opening in Chicago having little impact.
Chicago soybeans opened sharply higher on reports of an early frost possibly effecting the Brazilian crop, but European traders refused to follow.

"They (Chicago) are unbelievable, they went down on Friday because a couple of boats may be carrying some south American beans to the U.S. Now they come out with an early frost rumour in south America, we are not going to follow," said one.
Crude palm oil cif Europe closed $2.50 to $5 down while products were $2.50 down to $2.50 up with no further business reported.
Coconut oil closed $2.50 down to unchanged after Mar/Apr traded at $725 and Apr/May at $720 a tonne cif.
Palmkernel oil closed mixed at $2.50 up to $2.50 down in a tradeless market.
In soft oils prices were around 0.50 guilders down from midday with soy oil 0.50 to one guilder up and rape oil 0.25 to one guilder higher.
